methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: A region-wide collaborative effort to evaluate AI readiness suggests emerging distributed capacity-building infrastructure beyond traditional tech hubs, potentially democratizing AI fluency through deliberate peer learning networks in mid-sized metros.

signals.title: News Flash Archive - NPD E911 Division implements Artificial Intelligence (AI) system on non-emergency lines - City of Norfolk (.gov)
signals.signal_reading: Municipal government deploying turnkey AI solutions for call routing represents shallow but pragmatic adoption—distributed geographically but relying on vendor platforms rather than building deep internal capability.

signals.title: Roanoke coalition names Texas firm to study AI center plan - Virginia Business
signals.signal_reading: Commissioning specialized consultants to study an AI center plan signals aspiration toward concentrated excellence in Roanoke, but reliance on external Texas expertise reveals current capability gaps that could either resolve or reinforce depending on knowledge transfer outcomes.

signals.title: VCU partners with the Better Business Bureau to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-BBB partnership to bring AI support directly to Central Virginia small businesses creates distributed peer learning infrastructure, moving AI literacy beyond elite institutions into Main Street commerce through community anchor institutions.

signals.title: AI is already common in Virginia Beach high schools. Leaders weigh guardrails - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: AI already common in Virginia Beach schools yet leaders still weighing guardrails suggests proliferation without governance or deep understanding—shallow adoption spreading faster than institutional capacity to manage it effectively.
